notes: DISCOVERED during the construction-spending-2026-12-01 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). The residential leg is the largest single component of the proposer's aggregate — $871.2B of $2,157.6B SAAR, 40.4%, on the July 2026 data in CB26-140 — and it is the leg falling fastest (-7.3% y/y, -11.7% off its May-2022 peak) while office (+16.9% y/y, an all-time high) and power (+5.3%, an all-time high) rise. This calendar tracks the resale side of housing demand (existing-home-sales-2026-12-09, pending-home-sales-2026-12-17) and the residential supply side (housing-starts-2026-12-17, proposed) but has no entry for New Residential Sales at all — Census's own new-home demand print, 84 editions on the same seven calendars with zero gaps, and one of the Atlanta Fed's "Other releases" folded into a posted vintage when it lands on a trigger day, which 2026-11-25 is (GDP Q3 2nd estimate, personal income and outlays, M3-1). It stands six days ahead of the proposer and reports the same October 2026 reference month, so the two read the same month from the demand and the put-in-place side.
